requiredAssumptions.description: The request explicitly constrains operands to integers.
The request explicitly requires an exact product rather than an approximation.
The request explicitly calls for arbitrary precision, BigInt, or overflow-safe integer behavior.

contraindications.description: Do not apply to floating-point, decimal, approximate, probabilistic, or interval multiplication.
Do not generalize this profile to cryptographic multiplication or authentication behavior.
Do not apply when wraparound, saturation, SIMD, or other fixed-width hardware semantics are required.
Do not apply to a standalone arithmetic exercise with no software implementation context.

computationalFormulation: Represent signed base-10 integers without conversion through an unsafe fixed-width or floating-point type. Compute the exact product using a native arbitrary-precision integer when its semantics are explicit, or a bounded digit/limb convolution with sign normalization and carry propagation.
implementationPatterns: Parse and validate sign plus canonical integer digits before multiplication.
Prefer the language's exact arbitrary-precision integer type when available and serialize the result as a base-10 integer string.
For a manual implementation, use bounded schoolbook digit or limb convolution, normalize carries deterministically, and strip only redundant leading zeros.
Keep zero and sign handling explicit; negative zero is never a valid output.

verification.strategy: Parse both operands and the returned product with an independently selected exact-integer implementation, compare the complete signed decimal string, and include zero, sign, carry-chain, and values beyond safe fixed-width ranges.

risks.complexity: Schoolbook multiplication is O(n*m) time and O(n+m) space in operand digits; native big-integer complexity is implementation-dependent and must not be overstated.
risks.numerical: Conversion through IEEE-754 Number or an undersized fixed-width integer silently loses exactness or overflows; malformed signs, leading zeros, and carry propagation are correctness risks.

truthBoundary: This is a declared coding-transfer hypothesis and deterministic qualification surface. Mathematical mastery, profile validity, transfer qualification, live activation, and empirical coding benefit are separate claims; this profile is not checked in as qualified.
